## How to read these numbers

The service is a rate limiter, so a 429 is a correct answer and not a failure. That makes
a single throughput figure misleading, and two separate ones are reported instead:

- **Decisions per second** is how many requests the service made a rate limit decision
  about, allowed and denied together. This is the throughput of the service itself.
- **Allowed per second** is how many requests were actually admitted. This is bounded by
  the configured per-minute caps and by the number of users, not by the service's
  capacity.

With this run's mix of 16 users, the combined cap is 1,600
requests per minute, about 26.7 per second. Any offered load
above that is denied by design, so a high denial ratio here is the limiter working,
not the service struggling.

Latency percentiles cover every response, allowed and denied alike. A denial is cheaper
to produce than an admission, so a heavily denied run has a lower latency profile than a
lightly loaded one; the two are not comparable.

## Load profile

Open-model injection: the arrival rate is imposed regardless of how fast the service
responds, so a slowdown shows up as a queue rather than as reduced load.

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Algorithm | sliding-window |
| Users | 16 |
| Tier mix | 1 x ADMIN, 5 x PREMIUM, 10 x USER |
| Warm-up | 10 s at 50 req/s |
| Steps | 3 x 20 s at 50, 100, 150 req/s |
| Runs | 3 |

| Source at run time | committed, excluding this run's own output |

The load generator ran on the same machine as the service, so Gatling and the
application competed for the same CPUs. That caps the achievable rate and inflates
latency compared with driving the service from a separate host. These numbers are a
floor, not a capacity figure.

## Reproducing this

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

```bash
scripts/benchmark.sh --runs 3 --algorithm sliding-window
```

Raw Gatling output, the decision tallies and the captured environment are committed under
`docs/benchmarks/2026-11-10/`. This file is regenerated from them and should not be edited
directly.
